There is a specific shade of blue that only exists at four in the morning. It isn’t the velvet black of midnight, nor the optimistic gold of dawn. It is a suspended color, cool and weightless, hanging over the world like a held breath.

In this brief window, the city forgets its urgency. Traffic lights blink faithfully for empty intersections, casting rhythmic splashes of emerald and ruby onto damp asphalt. A stray cat navigates the alleyway behind the bakery, already aware of the warm yeast blooming inside brick ovens, long before the first commuter silences a blaring alarm.

To be awake now feels like sneaking backstage at a theater. You witness the scaffolding of daily life before the actors arrive. Street sweepers hum a low, mechanical lullaby, brushing away yesterday’s confetti of receipts and fallen leaves. A lone jogger passes, footsteps echoing sharply against rows of darkened windows, behind which thousands of distinct dreams are playing out simultaneously.

There is a profound, gentle sanctuary in this quietude. The demands of unread emails, loud headlines, and ticking clocks haven't yet staked their claim on the day. Everything remains pure potential, wrapped safely in indigo mist.

Then, almost imperceptibly, a bird tests a single, tentative note from a telephone wire. The deep blue softens along the eastern horizon, bruising into shades of violet and pale peach. The fragile spell thins. Somewhere down the block, a delivery truck’s engine turns over, clearing its throat in the chill air, and the world begins again.
